## What is this?

Floods, storms, earthquakes, heatwaves and droughts: somewhere in the world, a disaster caused by nature is recorded about once a day, and a few of them kill tens of thousands of people. This page is the overview of a series on natural disasters, and asks five questions:

1. **Which disasters happen most often?**
2. **Which kill the most, and has that changed?**
3. **Which affect the most people?**
4. **Where do disasters kill the most?**
5. **Where is the Earth itself restless?**

Each kind has a page of its own: [earthquakes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_EARTHQUAKES.html), [volcanoes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_VOLCANOES.html), [tsunamis](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_TSUNAMIS.html), [floods](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_FLOODS.html), [tornadoes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_TORNADOES.html), and wildfires, in [the world](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_WILDFIRES.html) and in [Greece](ILLUSTRATION_GREEK_WILDFIRES.html).

The data are downloaded when the page is rendered:

- **EM-DAT, the International Disaster Database** of the Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED) at UCLouvain, as published by Our World in Data ([Natural disasters](https://ourworldindata.org/natural-disasters)): the disasters recorded in the world each year, by kind, and the people killed and affected in each country each year since 1900. EM-DAT records only disasters that meet its entry criteria, and defines a disaster as "a situation or event which overwhelms local capacity, necessitating a request to the national or international level for external assistance" ([EM-DAT, definitions](https://doc.emdat.be/docs/data-structure-and-content/general-definitions-and-concepts/)).
- **The population** of each country, for deaths per person ([Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population)).
- **Earthquakes** of magnitude 7 or more since 1900, from the catalogue of the US Geological Survey ([USGS](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/)); **volcanoes**, from the Smithsonian Institution's Global Volcanism Program ([Volcanoes of the World](https://volcano.si.edu/)); and the **boundaries of the Earth's tectonic plates** ([Bird 2003](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001GC000252)).

**The kinds of disaster are those of EM-DAT.** A storm includes tropical cyclones (hurricanes and typhoons) and tornadoes; an earthquake includes its aftershocks and the tsunamis it causes; extreme temperature means heatwaves, cold waves and severe winters ([EM-DAT classification](https://doc.emdat.be/docs/data-structure-and-content/disaster-classification-system/)). **Deaths** are the confirmed dead and the missing.

## Packages

```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("plotly", "sf"))
library(plotly)

```

## The data

```{r download}
# a chart of Our World in Data as a table: one row for each country or region and each year
owid<-function(chart) {
  result<-read.csv(paste0("https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/",chart,
                          ".csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true"))
  return(result)
}
# EM-DAT: the people killed and affected in each country each year, by kind of disaster, and the
# disasters recorded in the world each year, by kind
deaths<-owid("natural-disasters-deaths")
affected<-owid("natural-disasters-people-affected")
events<-owid("number-of-natural-disaster-events")
population<-owid("population")
continents<-owid("continents-according-to-our-world-in-data")

# the earthquakes of magnitude 7 or more since 1900 (USGS)
quakes<-read.csv(paste0(paste0("https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/qu","ery?format=csv"),
                        "&starttime=1900-01-01&minmagnitude=7&orderby=time-asc"))
# the volcanoes that have erupted in the last 12,000 years (Smithsonian); the geological summary of
# each volcano has line breaks inside its quotes, which read.csv reads correctly
volcanoes<-read.csv(paste0(paste0("https://webservices.volcano.si.edu/geoserver/",
                                  "GVP-VOTW/ows?service=WFS&version=2.0.0"),
                           paste0("&request=GetFeature&typeName=GVP-VOTW:Smithso",
                                  "nian_VOTW_Holocene_Volcanoes&outputFormat=csv")))
# the boundaries of the tectonic plates (Bird 2003, as GeoJSON)
plates<-st_read(paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fraxen/tect",
                       "onicplates/master/GeoJSON/PB2002_boundaries.j","son"),quiet=TRUE)
```

```{r tidy}
# the kinds of disaster: the columns of EM-DAT's tables, their names in its table of events, and
# their names on this page
kinds<-data.frame(key=c("flood","extreme_temperature","extreme_weather","drought","earthquake",
                        "volcanic_activity","landslide","wildfire"),
                  event_name=c("Flood","Extreme temperature","Extreme weather","Drought",
                               "Earthquake","Volcanic activity","Landslide","Wildfire"),
                  label=c("Flood","Extreme temperature","Storm","Drought","Earthquake","Volcano",
                          "Landslide","Wildfire"))
# the charts with colours show the five deadliest kinds and put the other three together
kinds$group<-ifelse(kinds$key%in%c("volcanic_activity","landslide","wildfire"),"Other",kinds$label)
group_levels<-c("Flood","Extreme temperature","Storm","Drought","Earthquake","Other")
label_of<-setNames(kinds$label,kinds$key)
group_of<-setNames(kinds$group,kinds$key)

# a table of EM-DAT with one row for each place, year and kind; a year without a recorded disaster
# of
# a kind has no value there, which means that none was recorded: zero
to_long<-function(x,prefix) {
  y<-do.call(rbind,
             lapply(kinds$key,
                    function(k) {
    data.frame(entity=x$entity,
               code=x$code,
               year=x$year,
               kind=k,
               value=x[[paste0(prefix,k,"_yearly")]])
  }))
  y$value[is.na(y$value)]<-0
  result<-y
  return(result)
}
dead<-to_long(deaths,"total_dead_")
hit<-to_long(affected,"total_affected_")
first_year<-min(dead$year)
last_year<-max(dead$year)
recent<-2000:last_year

# the countries: rows with a code that Our World in Data puts on a continent (its regions have no
# code, or one that starts with OWID_)
country_codes<-continents$code[nzchar(continents$code)]
continent_of<-setNames(continents$owid_region,continents$code)

# the population of each place and year; the data end in 2023, and the years after it take the
# population of 2023
names(population)[names(population)=="population_historical"]<-"people"
last_population<-max(population$year)
carried<-do.call(rbind,
                 lapply((last_population+1):last_year,
                        function(y) {
  transform(population[population$year==last_population,],year=y)
}))
population<-rbind(population[population$year>=first_year,],carried)
```

```{r chart_style}
red<-"#d62728"
gray<-"#bdbdbd"
dark_gray<-"#6b6b6b" # also the colour of the notes
# the kinds of disaster, in the order of the stacked bars: the first five colours of a palette whose
# neighbours were checked for colour blindness, and grey for the rest
group_colors<-c(Flood="#2a78d6","Extreme temperature"="#eb6834",Storm="#1baf7a",Drought="#eda100",
                Earthquake="#e87ba4",Other="#bdbdbd")
# one hue, from light to dark, for the deaths per person on the map
reds<-c("#fee5d9","#fcbba1","#fc9272","#fb6a4a","#ef3b2c","#cb181d","#99000d")

# the source of a plotly chart, as a note under it, and the common layout
chart<-function(p,title,source,y_title="",y_axis=list(),x_axis=list(),annotations=list(),
                margin=list(t=70,b=90),note_y=-0.16,...) {
  note<-list(text=paste("Source:",source),xref="paper",yref="paper",x=0,y=note_y,xanchor="left",
             yanchor="top",showarrow=FALSE,font=list(size=11,color=dark_gray))
  result<-layout(p,title=list(text=title,x=0.02,xanchor="left",y=0.97,yanchor="top"),
                 yaxis=c(list(title=y_title),y_axis),xaxis=c(list(title=""),x_axis),
                 margin=margin,annotations=c(annotations,list(note)),...) %>%
    config(displaylogo=FALSE)
  return(result)
}
legend_top<-list(orientation="h",x=0,y=1.02,yanchor="bottom",traceorder="normal")

# numbers in the text
number<-function(x) {
  result<-format(round(x),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE,trim=TRUE)
  return(result)
}
percent<-function(x,digits=0) {
  result<-paste0(format(round(x,digits),nsmall=digits,trim=TRUE),"%")
  return(result)
}
one<-function(x) {
  result<-format(round(x,1),nsmall=1,trim=TRUE)
  return(result)
}
two<-function(x) {
  result<-format(round(x,2),nsmall=2,trim=TRUE)
  return(result)
}
thousand<-function(x) {
  result<-number(x/1000)
  return(result)
}
and_list<-function(x) {
  if(length(x)<2) {
    return(paste(x))
  }
  result<-paste(paste(head(x,-1),collapse=", "),"and",tail(x,1))
  return(result)
}
# country names that take "the" in a sentence
with_the<-function(x) {
  result<-ifelse(x%in%
                 c("Democratic Republic of Congo","Central African Republic","United States",
                   "Philippines"),paste("the",x),x)
  return(result)
}
```

**More disasters are recorded than before, which is not the same as more happening.** EM-DAT recorded `r events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year==1900]` disasters in 1900, `r events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year==1970]` in 1970 and `r events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year==2000]` in 2000, and since 2000 between `r min(events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year%in%recent])` and `r max(events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year%in%recent])` a year. Our World in Data warns that "the historical increase largely reflects improvements in data reporting" ([Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/number-of-natural-disaster-events)), so this page counts disasters only from 2000. Deaths are another matter: the great disasters of the past were recorded too, and the page follows deaths since `r first_year`.

**The population** of each country comes up to `r last_population`; for `r last_population+1`–`r last_year` the page uses that of `r last_population`.

---

## 1. Which disasters happen most often?

```{r often_numbers}
per_year<-sapply(kinds$event_name,
                 function(k) {
  sum(events$n_events[events$entity==k&events$year%in%recent])/length(recent)
})
often<-data.frame(label=kinds$label,per_year=per_year)
often<-often[order(-often$per_year),]
all_per_year<-mean(events$n_events[events$entity=="All disasters"&events$year%in%recent])
of_often<-function(label) {
  result<-often$per_year[often$label==label]
  return(result)
}
```

**Floods, then storms.** Since 2000, EM-DAT has recorded `r round(all_per_year)` disasters a year: `r round(of_often("Flood"))` floods and `r round(of_often("Storm"))` storms, `r percent(100*(of_often("Flood")+of_often("Storm"))/all_per_year)` of them. Earthquakes, droughts and extreme temperatures come next, `r round(of_often("Earthquake"))`, `r round(of_often("Drought"))` and `r round(of_often("Extreme temperature"))` a year, then landslides (`r round(of_often("Landslide"))`), wildfires (`r round(of_often("Wildfire"))`) and volcanic eruptions (`r round(of_often("Volcano"))`).

```{r often_chart, fig.height = 4.2}
often$label<-factor(often$label,levels=rev(often$label))
plot_ly(often,x=~per_year,y=~label,type="bar",orientation="h",
        marker=list(color=ifelse(often$label%in%c("Flood","Storm"),red,gray)),
        text=~round(per_year),textposition="outside",cliponaxis=FALSE,
        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.0f} a year<extra></extra>",showlegend=FALSE) %>%
  chart(paste0("Disasters recorded a year, 2000–",last_year),
        "EM-DAT, CRED / UCLouvain, via Our World in Data.",
        x_axis=list(showticklabels=FALSE,showgrid=FALSE,zeroline=FALSE,
                    range=c(0,1.15*max(often$per_year))),margin=list(l=140,t=60,b=50,r=20),
        note_y=-0.08)
```

---

## 2. Which kill the most, and has that changed?

```{r deadly_numbers}
world_dead<-dead[dead$entity=="World",]
# the deaths of each kind since 2000, the most first
since_2000<-aggregate(value~kind,world_dead[world_dead$year%in%recent,],sum)
names(since_2000)[2]<-"deaths"
since_2000<-since_2000[order(-since_2000$deaths),]
of_since<-function(k) {
  result<-since_2000$deaths[since_2000$kind==k]
  return(result)
}
all_since<-sum(since_2000$deaths)

# deaths a year per 100,000 people in the world, by decade and kind
world_people<-population[population$entity=="World",c("year","people")]
decades<-merge(world_dead,world_people,by="year")
decades$decade<-10*(decades$year%/%10)
decades$group<-group_of[decades$kind]
# the people of each decade, each year counted once (in the rows of one kind)
one_kind<-decades[decades$kind==kinds$key[1],]
person_years<-tapply(one_kind$people,one_kind$decade,sum)
decades<-aggregate(value~decade+group,decades,sum)
decades$rate<-1e5*decades$value/person_years[as.character(decades$decade)]
decades<-decades[order(decades$decade,decades$group,method="radix"),c("decade","group","rate")]
rownames(decades)<-NULL
decade_total<-aggregate(rate~decade,decades,sum)
worst_decade<-decade_total$decade[which.max(decade_total$rate)]
rate_of<-function(d) {
  result<-decade_total$rate[decade_total$decade==d]
  return(result)
}
last_decade<-max(decade_total$decade)

# the deadliest years of single countries: since 1900 and since 2000
country_dead<-dead[dead$code%in%country_codes,]
# the deadliest kind of each country and year, the deadliest first
place_years<-split(country_dead,list(country_dead$entity,country_dead$year),drop=TRUE)
worst_ever<-do.call(rbind,lapply(place_years,function(x) x[which.max(x$value),]))
worst_ever<-worst_ever[order(-worst_ever$value,worst_ever$entity,worst_ever$year,method="radix"),]
rownames(worst_ever)<-NULL
worst_recent<-worst_ever[worst_ever$year%in%recent,]
```

**Since 2000, earthquakes.** Disasters killed `r thousand(all_since)` thousand people from 2000 to `r last_year`: `r thousand(of_since("earthquake"))` thousand in earthquakes and the tsunamis they caused, `r thousand(of_since("extreme_temperature"))` thousand in heatwaves and cold, `r thousand(of_since("extreme_weather"))` thousand in storms and `r thousand(of_since("flood"))` thousand in floods. A few events make most of these numbers. The deadliest years of single countries since 2000:

```{r deadly_table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(country=worst_recent$entity[1:10],
                        year=worst_recent$year[1:10],
                        kind=label_of[worst_recent$kind[1:10]],
                        deaths=number(worst_recent$value[1:10])),
             col.names=c("Country","Year","Kind","Deaths"),align="llll",row.names=FALSE)
```

**Over the century, far fewer.** In the `r worst_decade`s, disasters killed `r one(rate_of(worst_decade))` people a year for every 100,000 people in the world; in the `r last_decade`s so far, `r two(rate_of(last_decade))`. The deadliest years ever recorded in one country were `r with_the(worst_ever$entity[1])` in `r worst_ever$year[1]` (`r tolower(label_of[worst_ever$kind[1]])`, `r number(worst_ever$value[1])` dead), `r with_the(worst_ever$entity[2])` in `r worst_ever$year[2]` (`r tolower(label_of[worst_ever$kind[2]])`, `r number(worst_ever$value[2])`) and `r with_the(worst_ever$entity[3])` in `r worst_ever$year[3]` (`r tolower(label_of[worst_ever$kind[3]])`, `r number(worst_ever$value[3])`). The last year in which disasters killed a million people or more in a single country was `r max(worst_ever$year[worst_ever$value>=1e6])`.

```{r deadly_chart, fig.height = 5}
decades$group<-factor(decades$group,levels=group_levels)
decades$label<-paste0(decades$decade,"s")
p<-plot_ly()
for(g in group_levels) {
  x<-decades[decades$group==g,]
  p<-add_bars(p,data=x,x=~label,y=~rate,name=g,
              marker=list(color=group_colors[[g]],line=list(color="white",width=1)),
              hovertemplate=paste0("%{x}, ",tolower(g),
                                   ": %{y:.2f} a year per 100,000<extra></extra>"))
}
p %>%
  chart("Disaster deaths a year per 100,000 people, by decade",
        paste0(paste0("EM-DAT, CRED / UCLouvain; population: HYDE, ",
                      "Gapminder, UN; via Our World in Data. 2020s: ","2020–"),last_year,"."),
        "Deaths a year per 100,000",barmode="stack",legend=legend_top,
        margin=list(t=110,b=80,l=60,r=10),note_y=-0.14)
```

---

## 3. Which affect the most people?

```{r affected_numbers}
affected_since<-aggregate(value~kind,hit[hit$entity=="World"&hit$year%in%recent,],sum)
names(affected_since)[2]<-"people"
affected_since<-affected_since[order(-affected_since$people),]
of_affected<-function(k) {
  result<-affected_since$people[affected_since$kind==k]
  return(result)
}
billion<-function(x) {
  result<-one(x/1e9)
  return(result)
}
```

**Floods and droughts.** From 2000 to `r last_year`, EM-DAT counted `r billion(of_affected("flood"))` billion people affected by floods, `r billion(of_affected("drought"))` billion by droughts and `r billion(of_affected("extreme_weather"))` billion by storms; earthquakes affected `r number(of_affected("earthquake")/1e6)` million. These are not different people: someone hit by a flood in 2010 and again in 2020 is counted twice. EM-DAT counts as affected the people who needed immediate help, together with the injured and the homeless ([EM-DAT, definitions](https://doc.emdat.be/docs/data-structure-and-content/general-definitions-and-concepts/)).

```{r affected_chart, fig.height = 4.2}
affected_since$label<-factor(label_of[affected_since$kind],
                             levels=rev(label_of[affected_since$kind]))
plot_ly(affected_since,x=~people/1e6,y=~label,type="bar",orientation="h",
        marker=list(color=ifelse(affected_since$kind%in%c("flood","drought"),red,gray)),
        text=~number(people/1e6),textposition="outside",cliponaxis=FALSE,
        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:,.0f} million<extra></extra>",showlegend=FALSE) %>%
  chart(paste0("People affected, millions, 2000–",last_year),
        "EM-DAT, CRED / UCLouvain, via Our World in Data.",
        x_axis=list(showticklabels=FALSE,showgrid=FALSE,zeroline=FALSE,
                    range=c(0,1.18*max(affected_since$people)/1e6)),
        margin=list(l=140,t=60,b=50,r=20),note_y=-0.08)
```

---

## 4. Where do disasters kill the most?

```{r where_numbers}
min_people<-1e6 # countries with fewer people are left out of the rates: one event decides them
# the deaths of each country and year, and the kind that killed the most
recent_dead<-country_dead[country_dead$year%in%recent,]
recent_dead<-recent_dead[order(recent_dead$code,recent_dead$entity,recent_dead$year,method="radix"),
                         ]
per_year<-split(recent_dead,list(recent_dead$code,recent_dead$entity,recent_dead$year),drop=TRUE)
yearly<-do.call(rbind,
                lapply(per_year,
                       function(x) {
  data.frame(code=x$code[1],
             entity=x$entity[1],
             year=x$year[1],
             deaths=sum(x$value),
             worst_kind=x$kind[which.max(x$value)])
}))
yearly<-merge(yearly,population[,c("code","year","people")],by=c("code","year"))
yearly<-yearly[order(yearly$code,yearly$entity,yearly$year,method="radix"),]
# each country: its deadliest year and kind, its deaths a year per 100,000 people, its people now
per_country<-split(yearly,list(yearly$code,yearly$entity),drop=TRUE)
country_rates<-do.call(rbind,
                       lapply(per_country,
                              function(x) {
  data.frame(code=x$code[1],
             entity=x$entity[1],
             worst_year=x$year[which.max(x$deaths)],
             worst_kind=x$worst_kind[which.max(x$deaths)],
             rate=1e5*sum(x$deaths)/sum(x$people),
             people_now=x$people[which.max(x$year)],
             deaths=sum(x$deaths))
}))
country_rates<-country_rates[order(country_rates$code,country_rates$entity,method="radix"),]
rownames(country_rates)<-NULL
small<-country_rates[country_rates$people_now<min_people,]
country_rates<-country_rates[country_rates$people_now>=min_people,]
country_rates<-country_rates[order(-country_rates$rate),]
top_rates<-head(country_rates,5)
world_rate<-1e5*sum(world_dead$value[world_dead$year%in%recent])/
            sum(world_people$people[world_people$year%in%recent])

# each continent: the deaths since 2000 by kind
continents_world<-c("Africa","Asia","Europe","North America","South America","Oceania","World")
continent_dead<-dead[dead$entity%in%continents_world&dead$year%in%recent,]
continent_dead$group<-group_of[continent_dead$kind]
continent_dead<-aggregate(value~entity+group,continent_dead,sum)
names(continent_dead)[3]<-"deaths"
continent_dead<-continent_dead[order(continent_dead$entity,continent_dead$group,method="radix"),]
continent_dead$share<-100*continent_dead$deaths/
                      ave(continent_dead$deaths,continent_dead$entity,FUN=sum)
rownames(continent_dead)<-NULL
share_in<-function(place,g) {
  result<-continent_dead$share[continent_dead$entity==place&continent_dead$group==g]
  return(result)
}
# the deadliest kind in each continent (of all eight kinds), as text
plural<-c(flood="floods",extreme_temperature="heat and cold",extreme_weather="storms",
          drought="droughts",earthquake="earthquakes",volcanic_activity="volcanic eruptions",
          landslide="landslides",wildfire="wildfires")
killers<-dead[dead$entity%in%continents_world[1:6]&dead$year%in%recent,]
killers<-aggregate(value~entity+kind,killers,sum)
names(killers)[3]<-"deaths"
killers<-killers[order(killers$entity,killers$kind,method="radix"),]
killers$share<-100*killers$deaths/ave(killers$deaths,killers$entity,FUN=sum)
# the deadliest kind of each continent
killers<-do.call(rbind,lapply(split(killers,killers$entity),function(x) x[which.max(x$share),]))
rownames(killers)<-NULL
killer_text<-and_list(paste0("in ",killers$entity,", ",plural[killers$kind]," (",
                             percent(killers$share),")"))
europe_heat<-dead[dead$entity=="Europe"&dead$kind=="extreme_temperature",]
heat_in<-function(year) {
  result<-europe_heat$value[europe_heat$year==year]
  return(result)
}
greece<-country_dead[country_dead$entity=="Greece"&country_dead$year%in%recent,]
greece_heat<-greece[greece$kind=="extreme_temperature",]
```

**Where one event struck a country hard.** From 2000 to `r last_year`, disasters killed `r two(world_rate)` people a year for every 100,000 in the world. Among the countries of a million people or more, `r with_the(top_rates$entity[1])` lost `r one(top_rates$rate[1])` a year, almost all in its `r tolower(label_of[top_rates$worst_kind[1]])` of `r top_rates$worst_year[1]`; then `r and_list(paste0(with_the(top_rates$entity[2:5])," (",one(top_rates$rate[2:5]),", ",tolower(label_of[top_rates$worst_kind[2:5]])," of ",top_rates$worst_year[2:5],")"))`. The `r nrow(small)` places with fewer than a million people are left out of the rates and the map: on a small island, a single storm makes the rate enormous.

```{r map, fig.height = 5.2}
classes<-c(0,0.1,0.5,1,2,5,10,Inf)
class_names<-c("Under 0.1","0.1–0.5","0.5–1","1–2","2–5","5–10","10 or more")
country_rates$class<-as.integer(cut(country_rates$rate,classes,right=FALSE))
steps<-do.call(c,
               lapply(seq_along(reds),function(i) {list(list((i-1)/7,reds[i]),list(i/7,reds[i]))}))
plot_ly(country_rates,type="choropleth",locations=~code,z=~class,zmin=0.5,zmax=7.5,
        colorscale=steps,marker=list(line=list(color="white",width=0.3)),
        text=~paste0(entity,": ",two(rate)," deaths a year per 100,000<br>",
                     number(deaths)," deaths in all; the worst year ",worst_year,
                     " (",tolower(label_of[worst_kind]),")"),
        hoverinfo="text",
        colorbar=list(title=list(text="Deaths a year<br>per 100,000"),tickvals=1:7,
                      ticktext=class_names,len=0.8,thickness=14)) %>%
  chart(paste0("Disaster deaths per 100,000 people a year, 2000–",last_year),
        paste0("EM-DAT, CRED / UCLouvain; population: HYDE, ",
               "Gapminder, UN; via Our World in Data. Grey: ",
               "under a million people, or no data."),
        geo=list(showframe=FALSE,showcoastlines=FALSE,showland=TRUE,landcolor="#e8e8e8",
                 projection=list(type="natural earth"),lataxis=list(range=c(-57,85))),
        margin=list(t=50,b=40,l=0,r=0),note_y=-0.02)
```

**Each continent has its own killer.** Of the people killed by disasters since 2000, the most died, `r killer_text`.

**In Europe, heat**, and its deaths are of another kind. For 2022 and 2023, EM-DAT's heat deaths in Europe, `r number(heat_in(2022))` and `r number(heat_in(2023))`, are almost exactly the heat-related deaths that epidemiologists estimated for those years, `r number(61672)` and `r number(47690)`, with statistical models of temperature and the deaths recorded in 35 countries ([Ballester et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02419-z); [Gallo et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03186-1)): estimates of the deaths that the heat added, not deaths counted one by one, as those of an earthquake are. In Greece, `r number(sum(greece_heat$value))` of the `r number(sum(greece$value))` disaster deaths since 2000 are such heat deaths, `r number(sum(greece_heat$value[greece_heat$year>=2022]))` of them in the years from 2022 to `r last_year`; for the summer of 2022, the first study found the second highest rate of heat deaths in Europe in Greece, after Italy.

```{r continents_chart, fig.height = 4.8}
rows<-c("World","Africa","Asia","Europe","North America","South America","Oceania")
continent_dead$row<-factor(continent_dead$entity,levels=rev(rows))
p<-plot_ly()
for(g in group_levels) {
  x<-continent_dead[continent_dead$group==g,]
  p<-add_bars(p,data=x,x=~share,y=~row,name=g,orientation="h",
              marker=list(color=group_colors[[g]],line=list(color="white",width=1.5)),
              text=~ifelse(share>=12,percent(share),""),textposition="inside",
              insidetextanchor="middle",textfont=list(color="#1a1a1a"),
              hovertemplate=paste0("%{y}: %{x:.1f}% of the deaths, ",tolower(g),"<extra></extra>"))
}
p %>%
  chart(paste0("Disaster deaths by kind, % of each continent, 2000–",last_year),
        "EM-DAT, CRED / UCLouvain, via Our World in Data.",
        x_axis=list(range=c(0,100),ticksuffix="%",showgrid=FALSE),barmode="stack",legend=legend_top,
        uniformtext=list(minsize=10,mode="hide"),margin=list(l=120,t=100,b=70,r=10),note_y=-0.1)
```

## 5. Where is the Earth itself restless?

```{r restless_numbers}
sf_use_s2(TRUE)
boundary<-st_union(st_geometry(plates))
quake_points<-st_as_sf(quakes,coords=c("longitude","latitude"),crs=4326)
erupted<-volcanoes[!is.na(volcanoes$Last_Eruption_Year)&volcanoes$Last_Eruption_Year>=1900,]
volcano_points<-st_as_sf(erupted,coords=c("Longitude","Latitude"),crs=4326)
quake_km<-as.numeric(st_distance(quake_points,boundary))/1000
volcano_km<-as.numeric(st_distance(volcano_points,boundary))/1000
# how much of the Earth lies near a boundary: an even grid of points over the sphere (a Fibonacci
# lattice), each measured like the earthquakes
n_grid<-60000
i<-0:(n_grid-1)
grid<-st_as_sf(data.frame(lon=((i*180*(3-sqrt(5)))%%360)-180,lat=asin(-1+2*(i+0.5)/n_grid)*180/pi),
               coords=c("lon","lat"),crs=4326)
grid_km<-as.numeric(st_distance(grid,boundary))/1000
bands<-data.frame(km=c(100,200,300))
bands$earth<-sapply(bands$km,function(k) 100*mean(grid_km<=k))
bands$quakes<-sapply(bands$km,function(k) 100*mean(quake_km<=k))
bands$volcanoes<-sapply(bands$km,function(k) 100*mean(volcano_km<=k))
in_band<-function(k,column) {
  result<-bands[[column]][bands$km==k]
  return(result)
}
```

**Along the edges of the plates.** The outer shell of the Earth is broken into plates that move against each other ([Bird 2003](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001GC000252)). The map shows the `r number(nrow(quakes))` earthquakes of magnitude 7 or more since 1900 and the `r nrow(erupted)` volcanoes that have erupted since 1900: they line the boundaries of the plates, above all around the Pacific Ocean. Within 300 km of a boundary, a band that covers `r percent(in_band(300,"earth"))` of the Earth's surface, lie `r percent(in_band(300,"quakes"))` of those earthquakes and `r percent(in_band(300,"volcanoes"))` of those volcanoes.

```{r restless_map, fig.height = 5.6}
# the boundaries as one line, broken (NA) between their segments
segments<-st_coordinates(plates)
breaks<-c(which(diff(segments[,"L1"])!=0),nrow(segments))
lines_lon<-unlist(lapply(seq_along(breaks),
                         function(k) {
  from<-if(k==1) 1 else breaks[k-1]+1
  c(segments[from:breaks[k],"X"],NA)
}))
lines_lat<-unlist(lapply(seq_along(breaks),
                         function(k) {
  from<-if(k==1) 1 else breaks[k-1]+1
  c(segments[from:breaks[k],"Y"],NA)
}))
plot_geo() %>%
  add_trace(type="scattergeo",mode="lines",lon=lines_lon,lat=lines_lat,
            line=list(color=dark_gray,width=1),name="Plate boundary",hoverinfo="skip") %>%
  add_trace(type="scattergeo",mode="markers",lon=quakes$longitude,lat=quakes$latitude,
            marker=list(color="#2a78d6",size=3+3*(quakes$mag-7),opacity=0.6,
                        line=list(color="white",width=0.5)),name="Earthquake, magnitude 7+",
            text=paste0(quakes$place,"<br>",substr(quakes$time,1,10),", magnitude ",quakes$mag),
            hoverinfo="text") %>%
  add_trace(type="scattergeo",mode="markers",lon=erupted$Longitude,lat=erupted$Latitude,
            marker=list(color="#eb6834",symbol="triangle-up",size=7,
                        line=list(color="white",width=0.5)),
            name="Volcano that erupted since 1900",
            text=paste0(erupted$Volcano_Name,", ",erupted$Country,"<br>last eruption ",
                        erupted$Last_Eruption_Year),hoverinfo="text") %>%
  chart("Big earthquakes and active volcanoes since 1900",
        paste0("USGS earthquake catalogue; Smithsonian, ",
               "Global Volcanism Program; plate boundaries: ","Bird (2003)."),
        geo=list(showframe=FALSE,showcoastlines=TRUE,coastlinecolor="#c8c8c8",showland=TRUE,
                 landcolor="#f2f2f2",projection=list(type="natural earth"),
                 lataxis=list(range=c(-60,85))),legend=legend_top,margin=list(t=80,b=40,l=0,r=0),
        note_y=-0.02)
```

```{r bands_table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(km=paste("Within",bands$km,"km"),
                        earth=percent(bands$earth),
                        quakes=percent(bands$quakes),
                        volcanoes=percent(bands$volcanoes)),
             col.names=c("Distance from a plate boundary","Share of the Earth's surface",
                         "Earthquakes of magnitude 7+","Volcanoes that erupted since 1900"),
             align="lrrr")
```

Earthquakes under the sea also cause most tsunamis. Each has a page of its own: [earthquakes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_EARTHQUAKES.html), [volcanoes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_VOLCANOES.html) and [tsunamis](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_TSUNAMIS.html).

---

## So, what does it mean?

1. **Floods and storms are the commonest disasters**: `r round(of_often("Flood"))` and `r round(of_often("Storm"))` a year of the `r round(all_per_year)` that EM-DAT records.
2. **Earthquakes have killed the most people since 2000**, `r thousand(of_since("earthquake"))` thousand, then heat and cold, `r thousand(of_since("extreme_temperature"))` thousand.
3. **Disasters kill far fewer people than a century ago**: `r two(rate_of(last_decade))` a year per 100,000 people in the `r last_decade`s, against `r one(rate_of(worst_decade))` in the `r worst_decade`s.
4. **Floods and droughts affect the most people**, billions since 2000; in Europe, by the estimates of recent years, heat kills more than any other disaster.
5. **The ground shakes and erupts along the edges of the plates**: a quarter of the Earth's surface holds nearly nine in ten of the big earthquakes.

**What this does not show.** EM-DAT records the disasters that meet its criteria, and more of them get recorded as time goes on; its recent heat deaths in Europe are estimates from statistical models, while those of an earthquake or a flood are counted. The people affected are counted once for every disaster that hits them. The rates per person leave out small countries, and one event can decide the rate of a country for decades. And the numbers count the dead and the affected, not what the survivors lost.

For the details, see the pages on [earthquakes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_EARTHQUAKES.html), [volcanoes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_VOLCANOES.html), [tsunamis](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_TSUNAMIS.html), [floods](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_FLOODS.html), [tornadoes](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_TORNADOES.html) and [wildfires](ILLUSTRATION_WORLD_WILDFIRES.html).
